title: When Environments Change
seo_title: Grade 3 Environmental Change Worksheets: How Living Things Respond and Solutions That Help
standard_text: Make a claim about the merit of a solution to a problem caused when the environment changes and the types of plants and animals that live there may change.
meta_desc: Free Grade 3 science worksheets on environmental change (NGSS 3-LS4-4): how plants and animals respond to changes, problems caused by roads, pollution and fire, and judging solutions with data. 100 practice questions with answers.
key_big: When environments change, living things are affected.
key_sub: Some survive, some move away and some die. People can design solutions, like wildlife bridges, and use data to see if they work.
body_html:
How to think about it

Environments can change. Nature causes floods, droughts and fires. People build roads, houses and dams.

When an environment changes, some plants and animals survive, some move away, some new ones move in and some die.

People can design solutions to help: wildlife bridges over highways, cleaning polluted water, planting trees, nest boxes and fish ladders. We judge a solution by its merit: does it fix the problem? Data from before and after is the best evidence.

Example

A new road cuts through a forest and deer are hit by cars. Name a solution.

Deer need to cross safely.

Answer: a wildlife bridge or tunnel

Example

After a solution, frog counts go from 8 to 30. Did it help?

More frogs live there now.

Answer: Yes.

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all animals change their bodies right away when the environment changes.
  • Thinking a change affects only one kind of living thing.
  • Choosing a solution without checking the evidence.

faq.q: What happens to animals when their environment changes?
faq.a: Some survive, some move to new places, some new animals move in, and some die.

faq.q: How can people help when an environment changes?
faq.a: They can build wildlife crossings, clean polluted water, plant trees, put up nest boxes and protect wetlands.

faq.q: How do you know if a solution works?
faq.a: Collect data before and after the solution, such as animal counts, and compare.
